interface.title: paplot (paplot-0.5.6) – 'demo' report: index, QC graphs, CA graphs, Mutation matrix
interface.stage_of_work: Looking at and quality-checking results after variant calling and structural-variant calling, before interpretation
interface.what_it_is_for: A set of static D3.js HTML reports, built by the paplot CLI from tabular result files, for checking per-sample sequencing QC, looking at where chromosomal-aberration breakpoints fall in each sample, and browsing a gene-by-sample mutation matrix that can be sorted and filtered without running the tool again.

data.note: The page was already generated for the 'demo' project when I arrived. QC covers about 30 samples (SAMPLE1–SAMPLE30). CA has 10 samples, shown as circos plots (SAMPLE1–10). The mutation matrix covers about 60 samples and 159 genes, with 11 ANNOVAR-style mutation types. paplot can also build mutational-signature and pmsignature reports, but this deployment did not generate them, so they are out of scope here. I uploaded nothing. Downloads made: paplot_qc.svg, paplot_qc.png, paplot_sv.png and paplot_mut.svg.

features.name: Overview strip with brush zoom, linked to several metric charts
features.general: Drag a range on a small overview bar chart so that every detailed chart below zooms to the same items. Sorting by any metric re-orders all charts together.
features.specific: On QC graphs, drag on the grey 'Average depth' strip ('Select a range to zoom in'). Charts 1–4 (depth, read length, mapped/total, depth coverage) zoom to those samples. The 'Select a sort type' dropdown with Sort / Reset re-orders all of them.
steps: Choose a metric in the sort dropdown and press Sort to rank items
Drag across a range of the overview strip
Scroll the linked charts, which now show only that range
Hover bars to read exact per-item values
Press Reset, or Sort again, to clear the zoom and restore the order
serves_tasks: Rank samples by one quality measure to find the worst ones, then restore the original order
Zoom in on a subset of samples in all linked charts at once
Read the exact values for one sample

features.name: Genome breakpoint histogram as a selector for small-multiple circos plots
features.general: Click or brush a region on a genome-wide frequency chart to pick the samples with events there. Then either highlight or hide the other samples' small-multiple plots, and filter by event class.
features.specific: CA graphs: click a bar or brush chromosomes on 'Distribution for breakpoints of CAs'. The per-sample circos plots are highlighted (yellow) or the rest hidden, set by the 'Style of selected graphs' radio. The Inter-/Intra-chromosome checkboxes filter both views. Changing the radio or a checkbox clears the selection; Reset clears it too and leaves the checkboxes as they were.
steps: Choose Highlight selected graphs or Hide non-selected graphs
Optionally untick Inter-chromosome or Intra-chromosome
Click a breakpoint bar, or drag a range over one or more chromosomes
Read which sample circos plots stay highlighted or visible
Press Reset to clear the selection
serves_tasks: Select a genomic region and see which samples have breakpoints there, then clear the selection
Restrict the view to one class of rearrangement
Choose whether non-matching samples are dimmed or removed

features.name: Gene × sample matrix with marginal bars and a category-legend filter
features.general: A gene × sample grid with marginal stacked bars (per sample and per gene). Ticking categories in the legend recomputes the cells, the marginal totals and the row order. Hover tooltips list the underlying records.
features.specific: Mutation matrix: untick mutation types (UTR3, UTR5, downstream, exonic, intergenic, intronic, ncRNA_*, splicing, upstream). Cells, the 'Number of mutation' sample bars and the '% Samples with mutations' gene bars update. Hovering gives Sample/Gene/type/chr:pos [ref -> alt].
steps: Untick mutation types to drop them from the view
Watch the matrix and both marginal bar charts recount (a spinner shows while it redraws)
Hover a cell to list its variants with genomic position and alleles
Hover a sample bar or gene bar to get the per-type breakdown
serves_tasks: Keep only the mutation categories of interest
Read the variant details behind a cell or bar

features.name: Multi-key sample sorter with automatic Gantt-chart layout
features.general: Build an ordered chain of sort keys for the columns (by ID, by total count, or by the presence of chosen rows). Alternatively, apply an automatic staircase ordering over the top N rows. The current key chain is shown as text, and a Reset button restores the default.
features.specific: X-axis sort-by: Sample ID / Mutation number / Genes radios. Choose a gene, then ASC or DESC, then 'Add sort key' (the chain shows as 'KRAS(DESC) -> APC(DESC)'). 'Automatic Gantt-chart Use genes top N' gives a staircase layout. Mutation number chosen while keys exist is appended to the chain. Changing the Y-axis sort resets these keys. X-axis Reset returns to Sample ID (ASC).
steps: Pick a gene in 'Select gene name' and choose ASC or DESC
Press Add sort key, and repeat for more genes to chain keys
Or enter N and press Gantt-chart for an automatic staircase
Or choose Mutation number DESC to order by burden (appended if keys already exist)
Press X-axis Reset to return to Sample ID order
serves_tasks: Order samples by the status of chosen genes or by mutation burden, and return to the default order

features.name: Row prevalence filter with live counts
features.general: Keep only the rows (genes) found in at least X% of items, up to a maximum number of rows. The page shows total and passing counts. The rows can then be ordered by count or by name.
features.specific: Genes filter: Rate (% Samples with mutation) and Display maximum (Genes), then Update filter. The text 'The number of filtered genes' updates (159 → 134 → 27). Y-axis sort-by uses Mutation number or Gene name, ASC or DESC; changing it resets the X-axis keys. Y-axis Reset returns to Number of mutations (DESC).
steps: Type a minimum Rate (%)
Type a Display maximum number of genes
Press Update filter and read the new filtered-gene count
Optionally sort the rows by Gene name or Mutation number
Press Y-axis Reset to return to the default gene order
serves_tasks: Order genes alphabetically or by frequency, and return to the default order

features.name: Export the current chart view as SVG or PNG
features.general: Save the current interactive state (sorted, zoomed or filtered) as a vector or raster figure.
features.specific: Export button → 'Save as SVG...' or 'Save as PNG...' on each report. Produces paplot_qc.svg/png, paplot_sv.png and paplot_mut.svg.
steps: Set up the view (sort, brush or filter)
Press Export
Choose Save as SVG... or Save as PNG...
serves_tasks: Download the chart as it currently looks, in vector or raster form
